- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or shows recent volatility, model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to lower end of forecast range.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects; cap subsequent forecast increases at +3% from peak.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags in adjusting; apply 1–2 day lag correction to forecast slope.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values (neutral/negative), model tends to underestimate true volatility; increase forecast standard deviation by 0.5–1.0% for next 3 days.
